Top-line: Oxley Strategic Computing is a defense-adjacent govtech prime evaluating Redwood Private for an air-gapped on-prem inference stack. Primary ask: run a 3-week on-prem POC in a classified-like DMZ with no internet egress. They are price-sensitive relative to on-prem TCO but prioritize certification and supply-chain assurance over lowest cost.

Key stakeholders: CTO (Lisa Oxley), Head of IT Security (Mark R. Hale), Program Manager (Maj. (ret.) Diana Cortez). AE (Riley Chen) owns deal; SE (Samir Patel) doing architecture. Procurement lead is Esther V. (gov contracts).

Quotes from discovery: "We need a stack we can put behind our classified DMZ — no callbacks outside the enclave." "Must show SBOM, pentest history, and HSM/KMS workflow we can audit."

POC requirements (explicit):
- Fully air-gapped install package (OVA/container tar) for isolated lab environment
- FIPS 140-2/HSM integration (KMS workflows; ability to bring-your-own-HSM)
- No external telemetry by default; configurable audit-logging to on-prem SIEM
- SBOM + signed binaries, vulnerability scan report, CVE process
- On-prem model store with ability to pin model versions; offline quantized model support
- Migration path for retraining/refresh using customer-approved supply chain

Performance targets discussed:
- Interactive operator chat: p95 latency <= 250ms for short prompts (local GPU pool, 8 GPU node test bed)
- Bulk embeddings: 800-2k qps target for batched jobs; prefer throughput over burst latency for daily ingest
- Failover mode: if model container unavailable, degrade to retrieval-only search-to-EMBED pipeline (no outbound calls)

Model preferences & routing:
- Prefer Redwood-verified open models (quantized variants) or validated customer-owned models.
- No SaaS-hosted fallback allowed for air-gapped workflows; fallback must be to smaller local variant.
- Expect documentation on kernel/quantization reproducibility across GPU generations.
